title: Temporal slot crediting for prefix microcache and GPU slab reuse
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Prototype and implement a session-aware microcache layer for prefix KV entries that assigns temporal "credits" to cached fragments. Credits decay based on request reuse and guide eviction and slab reclamation to reduce redundant KV rehydration across interleaved workloads. The goal is to lower cold-step latency and overall GPU memory churn while preserving continuous-batching throughput and latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: New microcache sits between request deserialization and global prefix store and can return prefix fragments without global lock acquisition for >=90% of targeted reuse cases.
Eviction crediting reduces rehydration of frequently re-requested fragments by >=40% in the mixed tenant synthetic workload compared to baseline.
End-to-end P50 generation latency impact <= +2ms and P95 <= +6ms on average for 1k concurrent streams after enabling microcache and crediting policy.
GPU resident slab churn (page reclaim cycles/sec) decreases by >=25% on the benchmark cluster under interleaved session patterns.
Design doc and implementation merged with feature flag and rollout plan; metrics and dashboard added to Console for the feature.
Unit and integration tests covering credit decay, tombstone reconciliation, and fallback to canonical prefix store are present.
technical_notes: Microcache concept: small LRU per serving-worker shard that stores pointers to GPU-resident slab cursors + a 16-bit temporal credit counter instead of full refcounts.

Credit semantics: increment on successful reuse within a sliding 5s window; decay schedule exponential-backoff to age entries that are not reused; credits influence soft-eviction order ahead of global LRU.

Tombstone handling: when a prefix fragment is evicted globally, write a lightweight tombstone marker in the microcache (0-byte marker on host mem) to avoid immediate rehydration on near-term requests; tombstones also carry a short TTL boundary to avoid permanent staleness.
Similarity hints: optional per-request simhash fingerprint lookup to allow approximate prefix aliasing and increase reuse across templated prompts, controlled by a runtime flag due to CPU cost.

Batch routing changes: continuous-batching runtime will consult microcache before including a request in a KV-prefetch path; hits avoid prefetch and can be injected into batch with existing KV cache tokenized state.

GPU slab reclamation: reclamation scheduler will prefer reclaiming slabs with low aggregate microcache credit to reduce rehydration tail; adds a reclamation score composed of credit weight + slab-occupancy-age.
Fallbacks: on microcache miss or tombstone TTL expiry, fall back to canonical prefix store path with existing dedupe logic. Feature behind feature-flag 'microcache_slot_crediting'.

2026-03-05 - Marco D'Angelo: Integrated tombstone fence; updated tests to validate fence semantics in compaction scenario.
2026-03-07 - Perf (Rohit Singh): First perf run shows 32% rehydration reduction; P95 latency increased by 5.8ms in extreme load (1.5x burst). Adjusted credit decay constants and re-ran.
